abstract: Inspects hardened perimeter barriers, biometric chokepoints, and intrusion sensor arrays
system_message:
You are the Physical security director (SECU), responsible for inspecting hardened perimeter barriers, biometric chokepoints, and intrusion sensor arrays, as well as tracking autonomous perimeter surveillance systems across subterranean archive repositories.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Autonomous perimeter surveillance（SURV）
information_points.content:
SECU-SURV-WJ6：Asset records for the Cairngorm Subterranean Repository indicate an infrared optical sensor density of 8 sensors/km deployed along the external facility perimeter fence line.
SECU-SURV-6Q6：Surveillance ledger records for the Pennine Bedrock Storage Annex show an infrared optical sensor density of 12 sensors/km stationed across the outer boundary fence line.
SECU-SURV-7A5：The Mendip Limestone Vault Complex maintains an infrared optical sensor density of 16 sensors/km along its external perimeter fence line.

information_points.title: Inspects hardened perimeter barriers, biometric chokepoints, and intrusion sensor arrays（PERIM）
information_points.content:
SECU-PERIM-WG3：For the Cairngorm Subterranean Repository, an assessment across the external exclusion fence and subterranean perimeter sensors confirms that perimeter intrusion detection compliance is true based on integrated seismic vibration, infrared fence line, and door strike sensor testing.
SECU-PERIM-97P：An evaluation of the Mendip Limestone Vault Complex's external exclusion fence and subterranean perimeter sensors shows that perimeter intrusion detection compliance is true, satisfying pass requirements for seismic vibration, infrared fence line, and door strike sensor integration.
SECU-PERIM-DT0：At the Pennine Bedrock Storage Annex, security audit testing across external exclusion barriers and subterranean perimeter zones indicates that perimeter intrusion detection compliance is false, having failed pass criteria for integrated seismic vibration, infrared fence line, and door strike sensors.
